newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up in dull trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up in dull trading on Monday on speculative buying from retail investors, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 19,970 yuan ($2,405) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened down at 19,800 and hit a low of 19,750.
January rose 10 to 19,900, February 60 to 19,950, March 30 to 19,930, May fell 10 to 19,910 and June 140 to 19,860.
Combined volume fell sharply to 37,730 tonnes from 76,400.
Copper opened lower but speculative buying from retail investors pushed prices up late in the session.
"None of the contracts could hold above the 20,000-yuan level despite speculative buying, which indicated further drops are likely," one trader said.
"The upward trend of LME stockpiles and a shortage of domestic institutional "hot money" at the end of the year will hurt the confidence of long position holders in the short term," he added.
"The thin volume showed most investor are staying on the sidelines with the short-term trend still unclear," a second trader said.
"Copper is likely to consolidate around current levels supported by higher spot copper prices for the next few days and then fall again," he added.
The current price of spot copper is above 20,000 yuan per tonne in Shanghai.
Aluminium ended down. The only traded January contract closed at 13,880 yuan per tonne, losing 30 yuan on paper-thin volume of 50 tonnes.
